mainTopic: The כהן גדול's share of the לחם הפנים, and how he was prepared for יום כיפור
overview: The amud opens by explaining a ברייתא that says the כהן גדול takes 'four or five' loaves of the לחם הפנים. The first answer says the two numbers come from two opinions. Under the רבנן he takes five, and under רבי יהודה he takes four. רבא says the whole ברייתא follows רבי, and that four applies when a delayed משמר is also present. The גמרא leaves רבא's reading as a קשיא, because רבי says 'always five.' A new משנה then describes how the כהן גדול was prepared for יום כיפור: elders reviewed the service with him, the animals were shown to him, and his eating was limited on the last night. The גמרא explains how a כהן גדול could be unlearned (in the בית שני the position was bought). It also explains why the goats were not shown to him. Finally, it lists foods kept from the כהן גדול and from a זב because they may cause an emission, and that list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'four or five' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means when it says the כהן גדול takes four or five loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'four or five'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא it just quoted. It wants to know when the כהן גדול gets four loaves and when he gets five, which sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave two numbers without explaining what decides between them. The גמרא wants to know what causes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The first-choice share the כהן גדול may take
The twelve showbread loaves divided among the כהנים on שבת

phrases.english: And what is 'four or five'?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא saying the כהן גדול takes four or five loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אַרְבַּע אוֹ חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the ברייתא's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Under what circumstances the כהן גדול takes four loaves and when he takes five.

steps.title: According to the Rabbis he takes five
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן split the twelve loaves six and six, so the כהן גדול takes half of twelve minus one, which is five.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, who say the incoming משמר takes six, the outgoing משמר takes six, and there is no extra payment for closing the doors, he divides from twelve. Take one less than half, and he takes five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It explains that 'five' follows the view of the רבנן, who divide all twelve loaves equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן give no bonus to the incoming משמר, so all twelve loaves count in the division. The כהן גדול takes one less than half of that total. Half of twelve is six, so he takes five.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment for closing the doors (an extra share for the incoming משמר)

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, who say:
The incoming watch takes six,
and the outgoing watch takes six,
and there is no payment for closing the doors,
he must divide from twelve.
One less than half: he takes five.
phrases.notes: He gets one whole loaf less than half, since he is not given a broken piece.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'five' half of the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five follows the רבנן, who divide all twelve loaves.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה he takes four
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives the incoming משמר two extra loaves for closing the doors, so only ten are divided, and the כהן גדול takes four.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, who says the incoming משמר takes seven, two of them as payment for closing the doors, and the outgoing משמר takes five, he divides from ten. Take one less than half, and he takes four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It explains that 'four' follows רבי יהודה, who takes two loaves off the top as a bonus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two bonus loaves are a separate payment, so they are not part of the division. That leaves ten loaves. Half of ten is five, and one less than half is four. The ברייתא's 'four or five' therefore reflects two opinions, not two situations.
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: four or five depends on the מחלוקת. Under the רבנן, twelve loaves are divided, so he takes five. Under רבי יהודה, ten loaves are divided, so he takes four. Either way, he takes one less than half.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
The incoming watch takes seven,
two of them as payment for closing the doors,
and the outgoing watch takes five,
he must divide from ten.
One less than half, and he takes four.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by explaining 'four'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Four follows רבי יהודה, who divides only ten loaves.

steps.title: רבא: the whole ברייתא follows רבי, who agrees with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא differently. All of it follows רבי, who holds like רבי יהודה that ten loaves are divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The whole ברייתא follows רבי, and he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new explanation of the ברייתא. He says it is one single opinion, רבי's, not two competing opinions. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's view, 'four or five' does not reflect a מחלוקת. רבי holds that ten loaves are divided, as רבי יהודה does, and that the כהן גדול takes half. That would make five the normal number, which leaves 'four' unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire teaching follows רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה. 'רבי יהודה' is a different, earlier תנא. Here רבי agrees with רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The whole of it is Rebbi,
and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the two-opinion reading of steps 2-3 and offers a single-opinion reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא follows רבי alone, who divides ten loaves as רבי יהודה does.

steps.title: Then why four? He should take five
steps.stepSummary: If רבי divides ten loaves and gives the כהן גדול half, he should get five, so where does 'four' come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what is 'four'? He should need to take five!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. Under רבא's reading, the number four seems to have no source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half of ten is five. If the whole ברייתא is רבי, the number four can no longer be explained as a separate opinion, the way the first approach explained it. So רבא must explain it some other way.

phrases.english: But then what is 'four'?
He needs to take five!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the whole ברייתא follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dividing ten loaves and taking half always gives five, so the ברייתא's 'four' has no explanation.

steps.title: Four when a delayed watch is present, five when not
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול takes four when a third, delayed משמר is also there and takes a share. He takes five when no such משמר is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (four) is where there is a delayed משמר. That (five) is where there is no delayed משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It explains that four and five describe two different situations, not two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes, because of a יום טוב next to שבת, a third משמר is also in the מקדש on שבת. It either came early or stayed late, and it takes two loaves, in addition to the two given for closing the doors. That leaves eight to divide, and half of eight is four. When only the incoming and outgoing משמרות are present, ten are divided, and half is five.

keyTerms.meaning: A משמר that is detained (staying over שבת because of a יום טוב)
Where there is / where there is not

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's approach: one opinion, two cases. With a delayed משמר, eight loaves are divided and the כהן גדול takes four. With no delayed משמר, ten are divided and he takes five.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where there is a detained watch,
phrases.notes: The detained משמר takes two loaves, leaving eight, so the כהן גדול gets four.

phrases.english: that is where there is no detained watch.
phrases.notes: Ten loaves are divided, so the כהן גדול gets five.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִיכָּא מִשְׁמָר הַמִּתְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (הא בכך, הא בכך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי, ten loaves are always divided, so the כהן גדול always gets five.
steps.terutzMaskana: A delayed משמר sometimes takes two loaves, which reduces the count to eight and his share to four.

steps.title: The math behind four loaves and five loaves
steps.stepSummary: If a delayed משמר is present, eight loaves are left to divide and the כהן גדול takes four. If not, ten are divided and he takes five.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a delayed משמר, the division is from eight, and he takes four. If there is no delayed משמר, the division is from ten, and he takes five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the numbers behind the answer it just gave. It shows exactly how 'four' and 'five' come out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Start with twelve loaves and remove the two given for closing the doors, which leaves ten. If a delayed משמר is there, it takes two more, which leaves eight, and half of eight is four. With no delayed משמר, the ten are split, and half of ten is five.

keyTerms.meaning: A watch of כהנים that was delayed and is still in the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רבא's approach work mathematically. Without it, 'four' would seem to have no source under רבי.

phrases.english: If there is a watch that is delayed —
he must divide from eight,
phrases.notes: Start with twelve loaves, take away two for closing the doors and two for the delayed watch, and you're left with eight.

phrases.english: and he takes four.
If there is no delayed watch —
he must divide from ten,
and he takes five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיכָּא מִשְׁמָר הַמִּתְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the arithmetic of the answer given in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (delayed משמר present or absent)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי, ten loaves are always divided, so 'four' looks impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Four' applies when a delayed משמר takes two loaves, leaving eight. 'Five' applies when no delayed משמר is present.

steps.title: Why does רבי say 'always five'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי agrees the כהן גדול sometimes takes four, why does the ברייתא quote him saying he 'always' takes five?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does it mean when it says, 'רבי says: always five'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's explanation from the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the whole ברייתא follows רבי, including the 'four' case. But the ברייתא ends with 'רבי says: always five,' which sounds like רבי is arguing against 'four.' The word 'always' does not fit רבא's reading.

phrases.english: If so,
what is the meaning of 'Rabbi says: always five'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the approach just completed in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the whole ברייתא, including 'four,' follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'always' shows that רבי disagrees with the 'four' clause. So that clause cannot be his.

steps.title: The question stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the challenge against רבא has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying the question on רבא remains a real difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the challenge is left standing. רבא's reading does not fit the wording 'always five.' The גמרא simply leaves it there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question remains unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבא, the כהן גדול takes four if a delayed משמר is present and five if not. But the word 'always' in רבי's statement does not fit this, and the גמרא leaves it as a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here is not a new question. It is the verdict on the previous question: the difficulty remains.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the challenge in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's explanation stays difficult because of the word 'always' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The elders read the יום כיפור service to the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: Elders of the court read the order of the day to the כהן גדול and ask him to read it himself, in case he forgot or never learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They gave him elders from the elders of the court. They read the order of the day before him and said to him: 'My master, כהן גדול! Read it yourself with your own mouth, in case you forgot or in case you never learned.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how the כהן גדול was trained for the יום כיפור service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court did not leave the service to chance. Elders reviewed the order of the day with him. They then asked him to read it aloud himself, in case he had forgotten it or had never learned it.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the day's service
My master, כהן גדול (a respectful address)

steps.whyThisMatters: The phrase 'perhaps you never learned' is exactly what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: They gave him elders from the elders of the court,
and they read before him the order of the day,
and they say to him: My master, High Priest!
Read it yourself with your own mouth,
perhaps you forgot
or perhaps you never learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the loaves discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Elders read the יום כיפור service to the כהן גדול and have him read it aloud himself.

steps.title: Showing the כהן גדול the animals
steps.stepSummary: On the morning before יום כיפור, they stand him at the eastern gate and parade the animals before him so he becomes familiar with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the morning before יום כיפור, they stand him at the eastern gate and pass bulls, rams, and sheep before him, so that he will recognize them and be used to the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another way they prepared the כהן גדול. He gets a hands-on look at the animals he will offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading about the service was not enough. On the morning before יום כיפור, they showed him the actual animals. This way the עבודה would feel familiar.

phrases.english: On the eve of Yom Kippur in the morning
they stand him at the eastern gate,
and pass before him bulls, rams, and sheep
so that he will be familiar and used to the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב יוֹם כִּפּוּרִים שַׁחֲרִית מַעֲמִידִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second kind of preparation to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animals of יום כיפור are shown to the כהן גדול on the morning before.

steps.title: Food during the week and on the last night
steps.stepSummary: All seven days he could eat and drink freely. On the night before יום כיפור, they limited his eating because food brings sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: During all seven days they did not hold back food or drink from him. On the eve of יום כיפור at nightfall, they did not let him eat much, because food brings sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this section by describing the כהן גדול's eating schedule before יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the week, he could eat whatever he wanted. On the last night, his eating was limited, because a full stomach makes a person sleepy. They wanted him to stay awake.

phrases.english: All the seven days

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל וּמִשְׁתֶּה,
phrases.english: they would not hold back food or drink from him,
on the eve of Yom Kippur at nightfall

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל הַרְבֵּה,
phrases.english: they would not let him eat much,
because food brings on sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים לֹא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the food rules to the preparation described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food and drink are free all week, but eating is limited on the last night so he won't fall asleep.

steps.title: Could a כהן גדול really be unlearned?
steps.stepSummary: Forgetting makes sense, but would we ever appoint a כהן גדול who never learned?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he might have forgotten. But 'perhaps he never learned'? Would we appoint someone like that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It questions the phrase 'perhaps you never learned.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can forget, so 'perhaps you forgot' is fine. But the כהן גדול is supposed to be outstanding, so how could he be someone who never learned? The גמרא is challenging how such a person could hold the job.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Granted, 'perhaps he forgot' — that is fine.
But 'perhaps he never learned' —
do we appoint someone like this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא שֶׁמָּא שָׁכַח לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּא לֹא לָמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'perhaps you never learned'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן גדול should be learned, so the court would never appoint someone who never learned.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the כהן גדול must be the wisest of the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to strengthen the challenge from Step 13. The ברייתא says the כהן גדול must be greater than his fellow כהנים in strength, looks, wisdom, and wealth. אחרים add that if he is not wealthy, the other כהנים make him wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: the verse says 'And the כהן who is greater than his brothers.' This teaches that he must be greater than his brothers in strength, in beauty, in wisdom, and in wealth. אחרים say: How do we know that if he has no money, his brothers the כהנים make him great? The verse says 'And the כהן who is greater than his brothers.' This means: make him great from what belongs to his brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a source to back up the question from Step 13. The source says a כהן גדול must be wise, so how could the משנה picture one who never learned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 asked a question based on logic: would we really appoint an unlearned כהן גדול? Now the גמרא adds proof from a text: a ברייתא requires the כהן גדול to excel in wisdom. אחרים disagree only about wealth, so both views agree that he must be wise. This makes the question much stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (a phrase that introduces a source used against a claim)
The כהן who is greater than his brothers (ויקרא כא:י)
'Others', an unnamed תנא or group of תנאים
Make him great, here meaning make him wealthy

steps.confusionAlert: אחרים are not arguing about wisdom. They only disagree about whether he must already be rich. Wisdom stays a requirement according to everyone.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
'And the priest who is greater than his brothers'
that he should be greater than his brothers
in strength, in beauty, in wisdom, and in wealth.
Others say:
From where do we know that if he does not have wealth,
his brothers the priests make him great?
The verse says: 'And the priest who is greater than his brothers'
make him great from what belongs to his brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a text-based proof for the logical question raised in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that an unlearned כהן גדול would never be appointed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא כא:י as requiring the כהן גדול to excel in wisdom

steps.title: First Temple versus Second Temple
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that there is no contradiction. The ברייתא describes the בית ראשון, when the rule was kept. The משנה describes the בית שני, when it was not always kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a difficulty. Here the ברייתא is speaking about the בית ראשון. There the משנה is speaking about the בית שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the question by saying the two sources describe different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the ideal law, and in the בית ראשון the כהנים גדולים actually met that standard. In the בית שני the standard was not always kept, so an unlearned כהן גדול really did happen. The משנה is preparing for that real situation. The law itself did not change; only how well people followed it changed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying the requirement of wisdom was cancelled in the בית שני. He is saying that in practice people did not follow it, so the משנה had to plan for an unlearned כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult.
Here, it refers to the First Temple;
there, it refers to the Second Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 13 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time period (בית ראשון versus בית שני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every כהן גדול was wise, so the משנה's case of one who never learned could not happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the בית שני, unqualified men were sometimes appointed, so the משנה's case was real.

steps.title: Proof that the position was bought in the Second Temple
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי reports that מרתא בת בייתוס gave ינאי המלך a large container of gold coins so that he would appoint יהושע בן גמלא as כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אסי said: מרתא בת בייתוס brought a half-סאה measure of dinars to ינאי המלך for his having appointed יהושע בן גמלא as כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to prove רב יוסף's point. In the בית שני, the job of כהן גדול could be bought with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the job could be bought, then the man who got it was not necessarily the wisest כהן. This shows how an unlearned כהן גדול could end up in office, which is why the משנה plans for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure equal to half a סאה (a large container)
A very wealthy woman of the בית שני period

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule about reviewing the order of the day with the כהן גדול reflects the בית שני reality, when the job could be bought. That is why the משנה plans for a כהן גדול who may never have learned.

phrases.english: As Rav Asi said:
A half-se'a measure of dinars
Marta, daughter of Baitos, brought in
to King Yannai
for his having appointed Yehoshua ben Gamla
among the High Priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer with a historical report.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the standard for the כהן גדול was not kept in the בית שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's report about מרתא בת בייתוס paying ינאי המלך

steps.title: A ברייתא adds that the goats were also shown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about the morning of ערב יום כיפור. A ברייתא teaches that the goats were also brought before the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On the morning of ערב יום כיפור,' and so on. A ברייתא taught: Even the goats were shown to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes a ברייתא that adds to it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists the bulls, rams, and sheep that were shown to the כהן גדול. The ברייתא adds the goats, the שעירים of יום כיפור. Since the ברייתא includes them, we now wonder why our משנה left them out.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats (the שעירים offered on יום כיפור)

phrases.english: On Yom Kippur eve in the morning, etc.
A tanna taught: Even the goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שַׁחֲרִית וְכוּ׳. תָּנָא: אַף הַשְּׂעִירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the unlearned כהן גדול and returns to the משנה line explained in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goats were also shown to the כהן גדול on ערב יום כיפור.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out the goats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה did not include the goats among the animals shown to the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, what is the reason he did not teach the goats?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה does not mention the goats when the ברייתא does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ברייתא. It is a request to explain why the משנה is silent about the goats. The גמרא expects a good reason for leaving them out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the author of our משנה)

phrases.english: And our tanna,
what is the reason he did not teach goats?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תְּנָא שְׂעִירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the gap between the ברייתא and our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why our משנה does not list the goats among the animals shown to the כהן גדול

steps.title: The goats would upset him
steps.stepSummary: Since the goats come to atone for sin, showing them to the כהן גדול would make him upset and discouraged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they come for sin, he would become upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה leaves out the goats because seeing them would discourage the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats remind him of the people's sins. That could weigh on him right before the most important עבודה of the year. So according to our משנה, they were not shown to him.

phrases.english: Since they come for sin,
he would become distraught.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּעַל חֵטְא קָא אָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The goats atone for sin, so seeing them would upset the כהן גדול. That is why our משנה leaves them out.

steps.title: But the bull also atones for sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The פר of the כהן גדול also comes to atone for sin, yet our משנה says it was shown to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the bull also comes for sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given. If animals that atone for sin are hidden from him, then the bull should be hidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה includes the bulls among the animals shown to the כהן גדול. But the פר of יום כיפור is also a sin-offering. So the reason 'it comes for sin' cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull (here, the כהן גדול's sin-offering bull)

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: פַּר נָמֵי עַל חֵטְא הוּא דְּאָתֵי!
phrases.english: a bull also comes for sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, פַּר נָמֵי עַל חֵטְא הוּא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the goats were left out because they atone for sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bull also atones for sin, yet it is shown to him, so the reason does not hold up.

steps.title: He can help the כהנים do תשובה, but not all of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The bull atones for the כהן גדול and his fellow כהנים. He knows them, so if one of them has sinned, he can bring him to תשובה. The goats atone for all of ישראל, and he cannot know about all their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bull is different. It comes for him and for his brothers the כהנים. Among his brothers the כהנים, if there is someone who has done something wrong, he knows about it and brings him back through תשובה. With all of ישראל, he does not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between the bull and the goats. The bull does not upset him, but the goats do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals atone for sin. What matters is whether the כהן גדול can do something about the sin. With the small group of כהנים, he can find out who sinned and help him do תשובה, so the bull only reminds him of a job he can handle. With all of ישראל he cannot, so the goats leave him feeling helpless.

keyTerms.meaning: For himself and for his brothers the כהנים
He brings him back through תשובה

steps.whatToRemember: Both the bull and the goats atone for sin. The difference is that the כהן גדול can help his fellow כהנים do תשובה, but he cannot reach the sins of all of ישראל. That is why only the goats would upset him.

phrases.english: A bull, since it is for him
and for his brothers the priests that it comes,
among his brothers the priests,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִיכָּא אִינִישׁ דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא —
phrases.english: if there is a person who has a sinful matter,
he certainly knows about him
and brings him back through repentance.
With all of Israel, he does not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּר, כֵּיוָן דְּעָלָיו וְעַל אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים הוּא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 and refines the reason given in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the two cases (sins he can help fix versus sins he cannot reach)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal that atones for sin would upset the כהן גדול, so the bull should also be hidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the goats upset him, because he cannot help all of ישראל do תשובה. With the bull he can help his fellow כהנים.

steps.title: רבינא's folk saying about a relative who becomes a policeman
steps.stepSummary: רבינא supports the idea that someone close to you knows your faults. He cites a folk saying: if your nephew becomes a policeman, don't walk in front of him in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what people mean when they say, 'If your sister's son becomes a policeman, make sure not to pass in front of him in the marketplace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a popular saying that backs up the last answer. The כהן גדול knows his fellow כהנים well, so he knows their sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the כהן גדול can bring his fellow כהנים to תשובה because he knows them personally. רבינא shows this is common human experience. A close relative in a position of authority knows exactly what you have done, so you should be careful around him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

steps.confusionAlert: This saying is not a new הלכה. It is only a real-life illustration of the reasoning in the previous step.

phrases.english: Ravina said: This is what people say:
If your sister's son becomes a policeman,
see to it that you do not pass before him in the marketplace.
phrases.notes: He knows your faults, so stay out of his way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the תירוץ of step 21 with a popular saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A close relative knows your sins, which fits the idea that the כהן גדול knows the sins of his fellow כהנים.

steps.title: Feeding the כהן גדול flour and eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's statement that they did not withhold food from the כהן גדול. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה בן נקוסא, who says they feed him fine flour and eggs to loosen his bowels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'All seven days they would not withhold' food from him. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה בן נקוסא says they feed him fine flour and eggs in order to loosen his bowels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the כהן גדול's food. It brings a ברייתא with one opinion about what to feed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן נקוסא wants the כהן גדול to empty his bowels before יום כיפור. That way he will not need to go out to relieve himself during the עבודה. His solution is to feed him flour and eggs, which loosen the bowels.

keyTerms.meaning: They would not withhold (food from him)
To loosen his bowels or digestion

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים לָא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: All seven days they would not withhold, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Nekosa says:
They feed him fine flour and eggs
in order to loosen his bowels.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים לָא הָיוּ מוֹנְעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of showing animals to the כהן גדול and turns to the משנה's line about his food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה בן נקוסא, the כהן גדול is fed flour and eggs to loosen his bowels.

steps.title: The Sages object that these foods cause arousal
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה בן נקוסא's suggestion. Flour and eggs would make it even more likely that the כהן גדול becomes aroused.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: All the more so, you are bringing him to a state of heat and arousal.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on the previous opinion. They argue that his solution causes a bigger problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole goal of the night before יום כיפור is to keep the כהן גדול from having an emission, which would make him טמא. Eggs and rich foods cause bodily heat and arousal. So feeding him these foods works against that goal.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁאַתָּה מְבִיאוֹ לִידֵי חִימּוּם.
phrases.english: All the more so, you bring him to a state of arousal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁאַתָּה מְבִיאוֹ לִידֵי חִימּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבי יהודה בן נקוסא's suggestion in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the כהן גדול is fed flour and eggs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These foods cause arousal, so they risk making him טמא. That defeats the purpose of guarding him.

steps.title: סומכוס lists forbidden foods using memory codes
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס, quoting רבי מאיר, says the כהן גדול is not fed the foods of the code אב״י. Others say the code is אבב״י. Some add that he is also not given white wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: סומכוס said in the name of רבי מאיר: We do not feed him 'אב״י'. Some say: not 'אבב״י'. And some say: also not white wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא gives a list of foods to avoid, written as short letter codes. The next step will explain what the codes mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view agrees with the חכמים that some foods are dangerous for the כהן גדול. It lists them as memory codes (סימנים). There are three versions of how long the list is.

keyTerms.meaning: סומכוס, a student of רבי מאיר
And some say it this way (another version)

steps.confusionAlert: אב״י and אבב״י are not words. They are memory codes, and each letter stands for a food. The next step decodes them.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא סוֹמְכוֹס אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Sumachos said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
We do not feed him 'Alef-Beit-Yod';
and some say: not 'Alef-Beit-Beit-Yod';

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא יַיִן לָבָן.
phrases.english: and some say: also not white wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא סוֹמְכוֹס אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the חכמים in step 24 by listing specific foods to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול is not fed the foods of the codes אב״י or אבב״י, and according to some, not white wine either.

steps.title: Decoding the food lists and the reason for white wine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the codes. אב״י means אתרוג, eggs, and old wine. אבב״י adds fatty meat. White wine is avoided because it can lead to טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אב״י' means no אתרוג, no eggs, and no old wine. The version 'אבב״י' means no אתרוג, no eggs, no fatty meat, and no old wine. Some add: not white wine, because white wine brings a person to טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the letter codes from the last step and gives the reason behind them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for the first letter of a food: א for אתרוג, ב for ביצים, ב for בשר, and י for יין. The reason given at the end shows the concern behind the whole list. These foods can cause an emission, which would make the כהן גדול טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity (here, from a seminal emission)

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason given here explains every food on these lists. They are all foods believed to cause heat and arousal.

phrases.english: 'Not Alef-Beit-Yod' means:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶתְרוֹג, וְלֹא בֵּיצִים, וְלֹא יַיִן יָשָׁן.
phrases.english: not etrog, not eggs, and not old wine.
And some say 'not Alef-Beit-Beit-Yod' means:
not etrog, not eggs,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בָּשָׂר שָׁמֵן, וְלֹא יַיִן יָשָׁן.
phrases.english: not fatty meat, and not old wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא יַיִן לָבָן,
phrases.english: And some say: also not white wine,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַיַּיִן לָבָן מֵבִיא אֶת הָאָדָם לִידֵי טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: because white wine brings a person to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא ״אב״י״ — לֹא אֶתְרוֹג, וְלֹא בֵּיצִים, וְלֹא יַיִן יָשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the letter codes listed in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forbidden foods are אתרוג, eggs, old wine, and according to one version fatty meat. Some add white wine, because it causes טומאה.

steps.title: A זב's emission can be blamed on food
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ברייתא about a זב teaches that his discharge may be blamed on food or on any kind of food. If so, it does not count as זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: With a זב, we may attribute his discharge to food, and to all kinds of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about a זב, because it also deals with foods that cause emissions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A discharge makes a man a זב only if it came on its own, not from an outside cause. Food is one such outside cause. So if he ate in a way that could cause a discharge, we attribute it to the food and he is not a זב.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with an abnormal discharge that makes him טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Here food helps the זב. It gives another explanation for the discharge, so he may stay טהור.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זָב תּוֹלִין לוֹ בְּמַאֲכָל,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: With a zav, we attribute it to food,
and to all kinds of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זָב תּוֹלִין לוֹ בְּמַאֲכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case where foods are connected to emissions and טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב's discharge may be blamed on food, so it would not count as זיבה.

steps.title: Foods a זב should not be fed
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר בן פנחס, quoting רבי יהודה בן בתירא, says a זב being checked should not be fed the foods of the codes חגב״י and גב״ם, or anything else that causes טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר בן פנחס says in the name of רבי יהודה בן בתירא: We do not feed him 'חגב״י' or 'גב״ם', or any foods that bring a person to טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives letter-code lists of foods to keep from a זב. The next step will decode them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the list for the כהן גדול. While the זב is being checked, we avoid foods that could cause a discharge. That way we can tell whether a discharge is real זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: That bring a person to impurity

phrases.aramaic: אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פִּנְחָס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא:
phrases.english: Elazar ben Pinchas says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira:
We do not feed him 'Chet-Gimmel-Beit-Yod' or 'Gimmel-Beit-Mem',

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כׇּל דְּבָרִים הַמְּבִיאִין לִידֵי טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: nor any things that bring a person to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פִּנְחָס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second view in the same ברייתא about the זב, listing foods to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב is not fed the foods of the codes חגב״י and גב״ם, or anything that brings on טומאה.

steps.title: Decoding the זב's food lists
steps.stepSummary: חגב״י means milk, cheese, egg, and wine. גב״ם means bean soup, fatty meat, and pickled fish in brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'חגב״י' means no milk, no cheese, no egg, and no wine. 'גב״ם' means no ground-bean soup, no fatty meat, and no fish in brine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the two letter codes from the last step. The next step asks what the general phrase at the end of the ברייתא adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for a food: ח for חלב, ג for גבינה, ב for ביצה, י for יין, then ג for גריסין, ב for בשר, and מ for מורייס. Eggs, wine, and fatty meat appear here and also in the כהן גדול's list. This shows they are the same kind of food, ones believed to cause emissions.
steps.whatToRemember: The night before יום כיפור, the כהן גדול is kept from foods that could cause an emission and make him טמא: אתרוג, eggs, wine, and fatty meat. A similar list of foods is kept from a זב who is being checked.

phrases.english: 'Not Chet-Gimmel-Beit-Yod' means:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חָלָב, וְלֹא גְּבִינָה, וְלֹא בֵּיצָה, וְלֹא יַיִן.
phrases.english: not milk, not cheese, not egg, and not wine.
And 'not Gimmel-Beit-Mem' means:

phrases.aramaic: מֵי גְרִיסִין שֶׁל פּוֹל, וּבָשָׂר שָׁמֵן, וּמֻרְיָיס.
phrases.english: soup of ground beans, fatty meat, and fish in brine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא ״חגב״י״ — לֹא חָלָב, וְלֹא גְּבִינָה, וְלֹא בֵּיצָה, וְלֹא יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the letter codes listed in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חגב״י means milk, cheese, egg, and wine. גב״ם means bean soup, fatty meat, and pickled fish.

steps.title: What does the phrase 'anything else that causes impurity' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the closing phrase of the ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירא and asks what it comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'nor any foods that bring a person to טומאה.' What does this phrase come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the last words of the earlier ברייתא and asks what extra foods they are adding. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two codes, חגב״י and גב״ם, already listed specific foods. So the general phrase 'anything that brings to טומאה' must be adding foods that are not on those lists. The גמרא wants to know which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include? A standard question asked about an extra or general phrase.
That bring a person to טומאה. Here this means foods that can cause a seminal emission.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כׇּל דְּבָרִים הַמְּבִיאִין לִידֵי טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: 'Nor any food items that bring one to impurity':
phrases.notes: A quote of the last phrase of the ברייתא from Step 28.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the general phrase at the end of the ברייתא whose codes were explained in Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which foods, beyond those in חגב״י and גב״ם, are included by the general phrase 'anything that brings to טומאה'?

steps.title: It includes the five foods listed in a ברייתא, starting with garlic
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes a ברייתא of the רבנן that lists five foods that bring a person to טומאה. The first one is garlic.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what the רבנן taught: five foods bring a person to טומאה, and these are: garlic...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the general phrase points to a separate ברייתא listing five foods that cause טומאה. The list begins with garlic, and the rest continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general phrase is not left vague. It refers to a known list from the רבנן. Those five foods are also kept from the זב being checked, even though they were not in the two codes.

keyTerms.meaning: That the רבנן taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
Five things. Here it means five foods.

steps.confusionAlert: The טומאה here is not caused by touching something. It means the food may cause a seminal emission, which makes a person טמא.

phrases.english: It comes to include that which the Sages taught:
Five food items bring a person
to a state of impurity,
phrases.notes: Meaning impurity caused by a seminal emission.

phrases.english: and these are: garlic,
phrases.notes: The list continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי הָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes the five foods from a ברייתא of the רבנן that bring a person to טומאה. The first is garlic.
